s15-graph-and-types.trick: A graph has vertices and edges; directed edges go one way, while undirected edges are stored in both directions.

s15-graph-representation-c.trick: For a sparse undirected graph, an adjacency list stores each edge at both endpoints and uses O(V+E) space.

s15-graph-representation-java.trick: This roadmap lesson uses Java collections; the equivalent C++ representation is a vector of neighbor vectors, one per vertex.

s15-connected-components-logic-explanati.trick: Start a traversal from each unvisited vertex. Every completed traversal marks exactly one connected component.

s15-bfs.trick: A queue visits all vertices one edge away before moving to the next level. Restart at unvisited vertices to include disconnected components.

s15-dfs.trick: Depth-first search follows one path until it cannot continue, then backtracks. Restart to cover disconnected components.

s15-number-of-provinces-leetcode.trick: Treat the symmetric connectivity matrix as an undirected graph. DFS from each unvisited city to count provinces.

s15-connected-components-problem-in-matr.trick: For an undirected adjacency matrix, BFS from each unseen vertex and collect the vertices of that connected component.

s15-rotten-oranges.trick: Put all initially rotten oranges in one BFS queue. Each BFS layer rots adjacent fresh oranges one minute later.

s15-flood-fill.trick: Start from the chosen cell and BFS only through cells of its original color, recoloring each when it is enqueued.

s15-cycle-detection-in-unirected-graph-b.trick: In an undirected BFS, a previously visited neighbor is a cycle only when it is not the current node's parent.

s15-cycle-detection-in-undirected-graph-.trick: During DFS, an edge to an already visited node other than the parent closes a cycle.

s15-0-1-matrix-bfs-problem.trick: Start BFS simultaneously from every zero. The first time a one-cell is reached gives its shortest distance to any zero.

s15-surrounded-regions-dfs.trick: Mark every 'O' connected to a boundary 'O' as safe. Afterward flip only unmarked 'O' cells to 'X'.

s15-number-of-enclaves-flood-fill-implem.trick: Flood-fill all land connected to a boundary cell. The land left afterward is enclosed and can be counted.
s15-number-of-enclaves-flood-fill-implem.space: O(R · C) queue and grid copy

s15-word-ladder-1.trick: BFS words differing by one character. The first time endWord is reached gives the shortest transformation length.
s15-word-ladder-1.time: O(N · L · 26), N dictionary words of length L

s15-word-ladder-2.trick: BFS assigns shortest distances and records every parent reaching a word at that distance. Backtrack from the end through those parents to list all shortest ladders.

s15-number-of-distinct-islands-dfs-multi.trick: Record every island cell as an offset from its starting cell. Translation-equivalent islands produce the same sorted offset list.
s15-number-of-distinct-islands-dfs-multi.time: O(R · C log(R · C)) worst case

s15-bipartite-graph-dfs.trick: Color each component with two alternating colors. An edge joining equal colors proves the graph is not bipartite.

s15-cycle-detection-in-directed-graph-df.trick: Mark DFS states as unseen, active, or finished. An edge to an active node is a back edge and forms a directed cycle.

s15-topo-sort.trick: In a DAG, append each node after recursively visiting its outgoing neighbors, then reverse the postorder. An active back edge means no topological order exists.

s15-kahn-s-algorithm.trick: Repeatedly take a zero-indegree vertex, output it, and decrement its neighbors' indegrees. Fewer than V outputs means a cycle.

s15-cycle-detection-in-directed-graph-bf.trick: Kahn's zero-indegree process removes every vertex of a DAG. If any vertices remain, they participate in or depend on a directed cycle.

s15-course-schedule-i.trick: Add prerequisite→course edges. All courses can finish exactly when Kahn's algorithm removes every vertex.

s15-course-schedule-ii.trick: Build prerequisite→course edges and record the order in which Kahn's algorithm removes zero-indegree courses.

s15-find-eventual-safe-states.trick: Reverse every edge and track original outdegree. Nodes with outdegree zero are safe; removing them may make predecessors safe.
s15-find-eventual-safe-states.time: O(V + E + V log V) including output sort

s15-alien-dictionary.trick: For adjacent dictionary words, the first differing letters define one ordering edge. Topologically sort those letters; reject invalid prefixes or cycles.
s15-alien-dictionary.time: O(total characters + E + K log K)

s15-shortest-path-in-ug-with-unit-weight.trick: Every edge costs one, so BFS first reaches each vertex along its shortest path.

s15-shortest-path-in-dag.trick: Topologically order the DAG, then relax each outgoing edge once after its source has its final shortest distance.

s15-djisktra-s-algorithm.trick: For nonnegative weights, repeatedly pop the smallest tentative distance. Ignore stale heap entries created before a better path was found.

s15-why-priority-queue-is-used-in-djiskt.trick: A min-priority queue exposes the closest unsettled vertex. Without decrease-key, push an improved copy and skip outdated copies when popped.

s15-shortest-path-in-a-binary-maze.trick: BFS on four-directional passable cells; each move costs one, so the first visit to the destination is shortest.

s15-path-with-minimum-effort.trick: Use Dijkstra where a path's cost is its largest height difference so far. Relax a neighbor with max(current effort, edge difference).

s15-cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.trick: At most k stops means at most k+1 edges. Perform k+1 Bellman-Ford rounds, copying previous distances so one round uses only one more edge.

s15-network-delay-time.trick: Run Dijkstra from the source in the directed network. The signal arrival time is the largest shortest-path distance, or -1 if any node is unreachable.

s15-number-of-ways-to-arrive-at-destinat.trick: Dijkstra computes shortest distances while each relaxation carries the count of shortest paths. Add counts when a different route ties the best distance.

s15-minimum-steps-to-reach-end-from-star.trick: Each residue modulo 100000 is a BFS state. Multiply by every allowed number, reduce modulo 100000, and mark each residue once.

s15-bellman-ford-algorithm.trick: Relax every edge up to V−1 times. A further improving relaxation proves a negative cycle reachable from the source.

s15-floyd-warshal-algorithm.trick: Try every vertex as an intermediate point. Improve i→j using i→via→j whenever both subpaths exist.

s15-find-the-city-with-the-smallest-numb.trick: Run Floyd-Warshall for all-pairs distances, count neighbors within the threshold, and prefer the larger city index on ties.

s15-minimum-spanning-tree.trick: An MST connects all V vertices with V−1 edges and minimum total weight. Kruskal selects light edges that join different components.

s15-prim-s-algorithm.trick: Grow a tree from one vertex by repeatedly taking the cheapest edge crossing to an unseen vertex.

s15-disjoint-set-union-by-rank.trick: Path compression shortens find paths; union by rank attaches the shallower root under the deeper one.

s15-disjoint-set-union-by-size.trick: With path compression, attach the smaller component under the larger root and update its size.

s15-kruskal-s-algorithm.trick: Sort edges by weight and add an edge only when its endpoints belong to different DSU components.
s15-kruskal-s-algorithm.space: O(V + E) for sorted edges and DSU

s15-number-of-operations-to-make-network.trick: At least n−1 cables are necessary. If enough exist, union connected computers and use one operation per remaining extra component.

s15-most-stones-removed-with-same-rows-o.trick: Treat every used row and column as DSU nodes; each stone joins its row to its column. Keep one stone per connected component.

s15-accounts-merge.trick: Union account indices whenever they share an email. Group all emails by DSU root, sort them, and prefix each group with its owner name.
s15-accounts-merge.time: O(M α(A) + M log M), M emails and A accounts

s15-number-of-island-ii.trick: Turn cells into land one by one. Each new cell creates an island, then union it with neighboring land and subtract one per successful merge.

s15-making-a-large-island.trick: Union all existing land. For each zero, sum the sizes of its distinct neighboring components plus one for the flipped cell.

s15-swim-in-rising-water.trick: Dijkstra minimizes the maximum elevation encountered along a path. The first time the destination leaves the min-heap gives the least required water level.

s15-bridges-in-graph.trick: Tarjan's low-link value records the earliest discovery reachable from a subtree. An edge u–v is a bridge when low[v] > tin[u].
s15-bridges-in-graph.time: O(V + E + B log B), B bridges sorted for output

s15-articulation-point.trick: A non-root vertex is an articulation point when one child cannot reach above it (low[child] >= tin[parent]); a DFS root needs at least two children.

s15-kosaraju-s-algorithm.trick: DFS finishing order identifies which component to process first. Reverse all edges and DFS in reverse finishing order to extract SCCs.
